subject: ironclad beetle
title: Scientists Drove a Car Over This Beetle Twice. It Walked Away

scenes.text: A car just drove over this beetle. Twice. It's fine.
scenes.keywords: car tire rolling asphalt close up

scenes.text: The diabolical ironclad beetle. Two centimetres long, and it can't fly. It never needed to.
In the lab it took 150 newtons before anything cracked. That's 39,000 times its own weight.
For you, that's like surviving the weight of 600 elephants stacked on your chest.
The secret is its back. The wing covers lock together like a jigsaw puzzle and peel apart layer by layer instead of snapping.
Researchers at UC Irvine ran a Toyota over it on a driveway. It played dead, twitched, and walked off.

description:
The diabolical ironclad beetle can survive being run over by a car. In the 2020 Nature study, its shell withstood about 150 newtons, roughly 39,000 times its body weight, before it began to crack; a car tyre applies about 100 newtons.
The wing covers, fused because the beetle cannot fly, meet in a jigsaw-like suture that locks under load and delaminates layer by layer instead of shattering. In the researchers' video a Toyota Camry rolls over the beetle twice and it walks away.
What else should we test it against? Comment below.
first_comment: Other beetles the team tested cracked at less than half that force. Engineers want to copy the jigsaw joint for aircraft parts. Which animal should we put to the test next?
